verdict.rationale: Marqeta's own card-transitions API lets ops change an existing card's state, which plausibly covers blocking a compromised card. Velocity and authorization controls are spend limits rather than fraud detection, and the webhooks are generic API-event notifications rather than suspicious-activity alerts, so neither earns credit. Missing for 10: network or proprietary fraud scores surfaced at auth time, suspicious-activity or fraud alerting, documented card reissue for compromised cards, explicit block/suspend semantics, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an ops user, the platform fights fraud on my issued cards — network fraud scores or its own models surfaced at auth time, suspicious-activity alerts, and tooling to block and reissue compromised cards

citations.quote: Use the `/cardtransitions` API to set the state of an existing card.
Creates a card state transition to set the state of an existing card.
